properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: md5@2.3.0 sits in the pnpm dependency graph as a transitive dependency of vite-plugin-web-extension@4.4.3 (build/dev tooling — used by the extension build pipeline, likely for content-hash fingerprinting), NOT in the shipped extension bundle. No first-party call site in application code. Keeping it as dependency inventory: the shipped toolchain exposes an MD5 implementation; if vite-plugin-web-extension ever uses it for anything security-relevant, that would be a live weakness. Dev-time, not run

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: XSalsa20-Poly1305 AEAD via @noble/ciphers' managedNonce wrapper (24-byte random nonce managed internally) is the DEFAULT cipher for every keystore create()d by the wallet-template keyring (create() hardcodes function:"xsalsa20-poly1305" at keystoreV4.ts:93), encrypting the user's seed/private-key secrets at rest in extension storage. Poly1305 is the one-time authenticator tag — symmetric, quantum-exposure is Grover-only. Authenticated encryption, so unlike the aes-128-ctr legacy path no separate

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 at the EIP-2335 decrypt path. The iteration count c arrives from the keystore file being decrypted (EIP-2335 floor is 2^18=262144; the repo's test vectors use 262144), so the static "below OWASP 600k" rating reflects the unresolved argument, not a shipped weak constant — no keystore is created with pbkdf2 here. Whether a low-c keystore is accepted is governed by the imported file, which is worth knowing for the posture record.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Unauthenticated AES-128-CTR branch of getCipher_() (keystoreV4.ts:181: aesCtr(key.slice(0, 16), hexToBytes(cipher.params.iv))) supported only for decrypting/importing legacy EIP-2335 keystores produced by standard Ethereum tooling; integrity rests on the separate SHA-256 checksum, not an AEAD tag. New keystores use xsalsa20-poly1305. CTR mode is malleable without the MAC — malleability of imported keystores is the recorded posture note.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge@1.3.1 ships a full crypto stack (AES, 3DES, RC4-era ciphers, RSA, X.509, TLS) but arrives here only as a transitive dependency of @devicefarmer/adbkit@3.2.6 — Android device-test tooling pulled in by the repo's dev/test toolchain. Its AES implementation is available to that tooling; the shipped extension never imports node-forge. Presence is the inventory question — recorded as available-in-build-toolchain, no application call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-128-CTR with a 16-byte key slice of the scrypt/pbkdf2-derived 32 bytes (key.slice(0, 16)) decrypts imported EIP-2335 keystores (the format standardises aes-128-ctr). 128-bit key leaves a 64-bit effective margin under Grover — below CNSA 2.0's AES-256 but standard-mandated for compatibility.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/hashes is the wallet-template's live hashing/KDF provider: sha256 (keystore checksum + PBKDF2 PRF), scrypt and pbkdf2 (keystore KDFs), and randomBytes/bytesToHex utils, all imported in src/background/keystore/keystoreV4.ts and exercised by keystoreV4.test.ts. Noble primitives are audited, side-channel-resistant and maintained — the posture baseline of this wallet. Declared in projects/wallet-template/package.json.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: X.509 support rides inside node-forge@1.3.1, transitively pulled by @devicefarmer/adbkit@3.2.6 (Android device bridge used by dev/test tooling — adbkit itself uses node-forge for its TLS/ADB handshake). No first-party certificate handling, CSR generation or PKI object exists anywhere in the repo's application code (no .crt/.pem committed, tls_sessions found no TLS session setup). Recorded as available-in-toolchain capability, not an application PKI asset.
